item: Comfort — the person in crisis (the `comfort` path)
angle: Behavioural design for daily habits (Fogg, Clear, Duolingo growth): the unit of reading, the trigger, the reward, the grace, the identity language, the return visit — applied to the one persona where habit formation is the wrong goal.
thesis: Comfort is the one path where the behavioural job is not to build a habit. Every other persona is a retention problem; this one is a duty-of-care problem with a retention side effect. So the design optimises three numbers instead of a streak: time-to-first-words (target under ten seconds from any screen), reachability (comfort openable from every path without changing the saved path), and human hand-off rate (how often someone in a hard season ends up talking to an actual person). Everything that keeps score, asks a question before scripture, or implies progress is removed. What is added is a door from everywhere, a region-correct crisis line the person can actually dial, a private route to a named pastor, and one artifact the person writes themselves — the Wysa "when it's bad" card, the single highest-used feature in crisis products. Week two is designed to look exactly like day two: no ladder, no graduation, nothing earned. The comfort path already gets the spirit right; the gap the evidence exposes is that it is a room you can only enter by declaring yourself a crisis case on a good day, and that once you are in it the safety net is a hardcoded English US phone number on the fourth screen.
principles: Presence before problem-solving. Scripture and audio come first; every question the app asks comes after words have been read (Lifeway: avoiding grief is always harmful; presence and acknowledgement rank above answers).

No score, ever. The streak is recorded silently and never shown, there is no count unless the person set one themselves, and the word 'complete' does not appear. Guilt-framed streak language drives opt-out and uninstall (cross-cutting finding 6).

No ladder. No graduation prompt, no upgrade condition, no 'ready for more' — the person leaves this path only by choosing to. There is no published evidence at all for a comfort-to-discipleship transition, so the app does not invent one (ruling: 'Feeling Stronger?' removed for good).
Crisis is not a persona you choose on a good day. Comfort must be one tap from every path, and taking that tap must not rewrite anything the person chose (research, Persona 6, journey bullet 1).

Show the line, don't disclaim. Only 35% of mental-health apps show crisis resources in-app while 81% carry liability disclaimers, and some show the wrong country's number (Crisis, 2021). We show a dialable number matched to the campus the person already picked, and we say plainly what this app is and is not.

Positive coping language only. God's presence and benevolent reframing; never 'have more faith', never a reason for the suffering. Negative religious coping predicts decline in longitudinal data (Pargament & Koenig).

The person's own words beat ours. The one artifact worth building is the card they write themselves — who to call, what steadies them, the verse they chose (Wysa's most-used crisis feature, >49% of crisis users).

Smaller unit, fewer decisions. Busyness is the number-one reason reading declines and the felt need is a smaller unit, not more content. Comfort's reading card currently asks for a translation choice before it shows a word of scripture; that gets collapsed.

Calm, not dark. The research says low stimulus; Ashley's locked look says light ivory, warm clay, paper-mode reading panel, no dark override. Calm is achieved by removing chrome — the gold AI aurora, the counters, the decision rows — not by dimming the app.

Every escalation is quiet and non-modal. The safety card appears under a reply, never as an interstitial, never blocking, never more than once a session. Anything modal in a crisis reads as being caught.

journey.day0: Two real arrivals. (a) Cold device: the app defaults to new_to_faith and shows the locked Day1Landing with its one quiet line, 'Not new to faith? Choose your path'. That opens the one sheet, where 'I'm going through something hard / Comfort scriptures. Nothing else asked of you.' is a tappable card, and one tap saves with source 'onboarding' and opens comfort immediately. That route is correct and unchanged — the landing is Ashley's locked screen and stays untouched. (b) The new and more likely arrival: a pastor, a friend or a hospital-room conversation hands over a link. `futuresdailyword.com/?comfort=1` opens the Comfort Now overlay directly on arrival — today's verse, Listen, the chapter, the talk-to-someone row — writing nothing to dw_setup, crediting no plan day, changing no path. The person gets words in under ten seconds and has made no declarations about themselves. This is the single most useful new lever a campus pastor gets.
journey.first_session: Greeting (date-keyed, never visit-keyed: 'You are not alone, {name}'). Then the day's verse with the Pray toggle. Then the reading card, where Listen is now the primary control above the chapter and the chapter is already loaded — audio first, one passage, low stimulus. They read or listen for as long as they want; the only control is 'I've finished reading'. Then the devotion in Ashley's voice. Then, once, the post-read ask: read another, or that's enough for today. At the foot, always, quiet and unstyled as an alarm: 'Talk to someone' with 'Ask a pastor to pray' and the region-correct line. Once, on first use, one line of disclosure: this is scripture and a church, not counselling. No push modal, no email gate stacked on top — comfort stays excluded from the automatic PushOptIn.
journey.return_visit: Their 'when it's bad' card sits at the top if they made one — the first thing on screen is their own handwriting, not ours. The verse and chapter have moved on by local date. If they set a daily amount, the app serves that many and never re-asks. One small addition: alongside today's chapter, a single one-tap 'Yesterday's chapter' — the research line 'still here, same verse or a new one'. There is no welcome-back message, because a welcome-back implies absence was noticed.
journey.week2: Nothing new. That is the design, and it is deliberate: week two is built to look like day two. No milestone, no 'you've been here 14 days', no suggestion that this season should be over. The only things that changed are the chapter (14 of a 30-chapter rotation) and, if they wrote one, the card at the top. Any behaviour-triggered escalation at week two — surfacing the pastor row more prominently because someone has been in crisis a while — was considered and rejected: it reads as surveillance, and there is no evidence for the timing.
journey.missed_day: Invisible. recordStreakToday() still runs on mount and is idempotent, so the streak object stays consistent for sync, but comfort never renders it and never mentions it. No 'we missed you', no streak-repair message, no re-engagement push about the gap. If the one reminder is on, tomorrow's reminder is byte-identical to yesterday's and references nothing about absence. The greeting rotates on day-of-month, not on visit count, so a person returning after nine days sees a greeting that has no idea they were gone.
journey.seasonal: The calendar move for every other persona is a time-boxed shared challenge (YouVersion's 3M January plan starts, Hallow's 5M-concurrent Lent). For comfort it is the exact opposite: the hard dates. `public/comfort.json` carries an optional `dates` block mapping a local date to a chapter override plus one line — so a campus pastor can set 24 December to Psalm 121 with 'Christmas is hard for a lot of people. This one is for you.', or Mother's Day, Father's Day, Easter Saturday, the anniversary of a local loss. No countdown, no participation count, no shared total. The 'reading today' live count planned for the seasonal church-wide read must never render on this path.

comfort_access: Four doors, none of which change the saved path. (1) A 'Need comfort now' heart pill in the Home header beside the existing PathSwatch, rendered for every persona except comfort itself — the PathSwatch already proves that slot works on every path. (2) A 'Talk to someone' row on the More screen for every persona, which also carries the crisis line. (3) The safety card under a Bible AI reply, a journal save or a prayer post on any path. (4) A shareable link, `futuresdailyword.com/?comfort=1`, that opens the overlay on arrival — the door a campus pastor can text to someone in a hospital car park. All four open the same Comfort Now overlay, which must obey three rulings exactly: it uses useSubView alone with no useModalA11y or aria-modal, so the nested focus traps that broke keyboard and Android back do not come back; it stays mounted with a live `open` prop rather than being conditionally mounted, so it does not orphan a history entry per close; and it is credit-free — it bypasses handleRead entirely, stamps no dw_reading_done, touches no dw_pathway_progress, and never calls saveSetup, exactly as the arrival-seed ruling requires of every persona-gated open. A single quiet foot link, 'Make this my path', is the only way it can lead to a saveSetup, and that goes through the normal ChoosePathSheet commit with source 'settings' so it stamps as a real choice.
reminders: One a day, opt-in, offered once, in context, never modal. The automatic full-screen PushOptIn stays banned for comfort — a system permission dialog immediately after someone reads Psalm 23 in a hard hour is the wrong moment, and the live exclusion at App.tsx:311-319 is correct. Instead the offer appears as two buttons at the post-read 'done' state, after they have evidence of what the app is worth: 'Want one quiet reminder tomorrow? One a day, around this time. No counting, no streaks.' If they accept, the subscription hour is the local hour they actually read today — behaviour-inferred timing rather than a picker, which is the Duolingo pattern and the one place the cross-cutting research is unambiguous. If they decline, dw_comfort_reminder_asked is set and it is never asked again. Devices without push fall through to the existing openCalendarReminder hand-off. Comfort gets its own template set, separate from the generic EN/ID arrays in push-send.js, and the copy is bounded by one rule that should be enforced by a test: no reference to days, streaks, catching up, missing, or duty. 'A word for you — "{verse}", {passage} is here when you want it.' The reminder after a nine-day gap is byte-identical to the reminder after a one-day gap. Guilt-framed reminders are the documented driver of notification opt-out and uninstall, and this is the persona least able to absorb one.
instrumentation: comfort_open — detail: source (home | comfort_now_pill | more | ai_safety_card | deeplink). The reachability number: what fraction of comfort sessions arrive from a path other than comfort. This is the primary proof that the door-from-everywhere move worked.
comfort_listen — detail: passage. Proves the audio-first reorder: listen rate before vs after Listen moves above the text.
comfort_finished — detail: passage. The soft completion, replacing any reliance on the generic dw_reading_done stamp for this path.
comfort_daily_set — detail: n. How many people choose a shape for themselves rather than being given one.
comfort_card_saved and comfort_card_opened — the Wysa comparison. Opened-per-saved is the number that says whether the card is an artifact or a form.
care_line_shown — detail: region. care_line_tapped — detail: region. Together these are the duty-of-care numbers, and the region detail is what catches a wrong-country line before someone dials it.
pastor_prayer_sent — detail: campus. The human hand-off rate, and the number that tells a campus whether anyone is actually watching that inbox.

safety_prompt_shown — detail: surface (ai | journal | prayer). safety_prompt_dismissed. Shown-to-dismissed ratio is the false-positive proxy; a dismissal rate above about 80% means the keyword list is too wide and should be narrowed.
comfort_reminder_on and comfort_reminder_off — opt-in rate at the done state, and the churn out of it. An opt-out rate climbing over time is the early warning that the copy has drifted toward duty.

app_open gains a `path` detail — the only way to get D1/D7/D30 by path, which the research names as the single biggest gap and the first thing to build, because no public source will ever supply it for a Bible app.
A nightly rollup, per path: sessions, distinct days active, D1/D7/D30, median session length, comfort_open by source. Descriptive only — nothing in it may drive a nudge on this path.
self_serve_levers: public/comfort.json — the chapter rotation, the verse-and-guided-prayer pairs, and the devotions, in one file, fetched network-first with the bundled src/data/comfort.ts as the offline fallback. Today a pastor changing one devotion needs a TSX edit; after this they edit one JSON file. Non-negotiable condition: this is a new asset class under the /books service-worker trap, so it must be network-first with cache as offline fallback only, and CACHE_NAME, STATIC_CACHE and SW_VERSION bump together, or every returning user reads last month's devotion forever.

public/comfort.json → `dates` block — an optional date-to-chapter override with one line of copy, so a campus pastor sets Christmas Eve, Mother's Day, Father's Day or a local anniversary without a developer. This is the whole seasonal design for this path.

public/care.json — per region: the helpline label, the number, and the tel: href. Per campus: the care email address and the name of the person who receives a private prayer request. This is the lever behind 'who at each campus receives the prayer request', and it means a campus that changes its care pastor changes a line of JSON, not a component.

The comfort push template set, read from comfort.json at send time by push-send.js with a hardcoded fallback — so the reminder wording is editable too, instead of joining the seven-variant arrays that currently need a function redeploy.
The daily reading amount (1, 2 or 3 chapters) — already user-owned via dw_comfort_daily and synced; unchanged.
The campus chip in the Home header — already user-owned, and it is now load-bearing, because it is what resolves the crisis line to the right country.
The ?comfort=1 link — a campus pastor's own distribution lever, needing nothing from anyone: one URL that opens scripture and a helpline in one tap.

open_decisions: The crisis line for Indonesia and Brazil. US 988 and Australia's Lifeline 13 11 14 are drafted and NZ 1737 is held for a future campus, but five Indonesian campuses and Futures Rio have no line drafted and this is explicitly named as Ashley's decision in the research. Until he rules, those regions must show the findahelpline fallback rather than a guessed number — the exact failure the Crisis paper documents.

Who at each campus receives a private prayer request, by name, and what the app is allowed to promise. 'Someone from {campus} will read it' is the safe default; 'someone will get back to you' is a promise the app cannot keep on its own. This gates the whole feature: shipping a private request into an unwatched inbox is worse than not shipping it.

Whether the 'Need comfort now' pill goes in the Home header for the other four personas, or lives only on the More screen. The header is part of the locked look and this adds a control to it for four of five paths.

Whether a private prayer request may be sent without an email address. The public wall requires one today; someone in a hard hour may not want to identify themselves, and requiring an account here loses the people who most need the hand-off.

Whether comfort gets a push reminder at all. Comfort is deliberately excluded from push onboarding today, and the offer designed here is deliberately small and in-context — but it is still a notification to someone in crisis, and that is his call, not a designer's.
The exact wording of the not-counselling disclosure — his plain line, or the church's legal wording. Plain reads better; legal may be required.
Whether the seasonal hard-dates block is his to author centrally or each campus pastor's to set locally. The lever supports both; the governance is a decision.
risks: False positives on the crisis keyword list. 'This deadline is killing me' triggering a suicide hotline card is patronising and drives people off the feature. Mitigation: a narrow, high-precision list, explicit negative guards for the common idioms, one non-modal card, one per session, easy dismiss — and safety_prompt_dismissed watched as the false-positive proxy, narrowing the list if dismissal runs above roughly 80%.

Duty of care created and not met. A private 'ask a pastor to pray' sets an expectation that a human is on the other end. If no named person is watching that inbox at a campus, the app has made a promise it cannot keep, to the people least able to absorb a second disappointment. This is why the named-recipient decision gates the ship, not just the copy.
A wrong-country helpline. Indonesian and Brazilian campuses have no drafted line; a default to 988 would reproduce the exact documented failure. The fallback must be structural, not a TODO.

Detection privacy. Crisis-language matching must run entirely client-side on text that is never logged, never sent for classification, and never stored as a flag on the person's record. A server round-trip to decide whether someone is suicidal is a data liability and would change what this app is.

Comfort Now leaking into other personas' progress. It is reachable from four paths; if it stamps dw_reading_done, advances a plan day, or writes dw_setup, it corrupts the exact records the arrival-seed and never-rebuild-from-React-state rulings were written to protect. This needs a test, not a code review.

Reminder copy drift. Comfort's push templates are one PR away from picking up 'don't break your streak'. A test asserting the comfort set contains none of day, streak, missed, catch up, or back is cheap insurance.

The service-worker content trap. Moving devotions and verses to JSON without making that class network-first means every returning user reads stale content indefinitely, and the failure is invisible from a fresh browser — which is how it was missed the first time.

Scope creep past the preview gate. This is a visual and IA change to the opening screen for five paths. The temptation will be to merge the safe-looking parts first. The whole set goes behind one preview link and waits.

Comfort is the only path still painted in the pre-relook indigo, which means the repaint is unavoidable if it is touched at all — and a repaint of a comfort screen is exactly the class of change that got a rebuild reverted in September. Preview, then his word.

build_steps.step: Instrumentation first — it is the research's own item 1, and every later step is unmeasurable without it. Add the new comfort, care and safety events to the TRACKED_EVENTS allowlist, add a `path` detail to app_open, and add a per-path rollup to the dashboard function.
build_steps.check: Run one scripted comfort session end to end on localhost; every new event appears in the Supabase activity table and in the dashboard's per-path panel within one refresh. An event name not on the allowlist is silently dropped, so assert presence, never absence of an error.

build_steps.step: Content out of code. Move COMFORT_CHAPTERS, COMFORT_DEVOTIONS, COMFORT_VERSES and GUIDED_PRAYERS into one public/comfort.json with an optional `dates` block; keep the existing TS exports as the bundled offline fallback; add the loader. Then make the service worker treat /comfort.json (and /care.json) network-first with cache as offline fallback only, and bump the three version constants together.
